justification: The trusted payee inventory is computed by host code (banking_inventories) that the Aletheia user writes; identical edit: IBANs scraped from free-text transaction subjects are added to `payees`.

Policy relaxed from exact membership to 'contained in some quoted string'; Aletheia's built-in s.mentions(k,x) is exactly any(x in q for q in inventory k). Difference: s.mentions rejects the empty string by language definition, so the empty-password sub-case of the original defect is not reproducible.

justification: Aletheia match has no or-patterns, so 'merge Update and Retarget into one rule' is written as giving Retarget the same id-only rule as Update; the recipient check is dropped, same data flow.

justification: New Cancel variant wired into Write (plan schema), a Bank.Transfer tool (effect->capability), the commit dispatch and the host binding. Aletheia policies have no fallback/default arm (match must be exhaustive), so 'flip the default to allow' is written as the allow-all rule `Cancel { id } => true` for the new variant; unlike the Python fallback it cannot also cover future variants.

edits.old: refine again by SafePlan retry 1 else {
edits.new: refine again by SafePlan keeping writes by SafeWrite retry 1 else {

justification: Aletheia has no agent-wide mode variable; the mode is the per-refine `keeping` clause. Same mistake: the retry gate after a rejection uses the agent's keeping (prune) semantics instead of all-or-nothing. (`as` binding is only permitted in a let, so the clause is written without it.)

Endorsement and the single commit point are language machinery: Endorsed labels are checked by athc (ath-check) and `commit`/endorse journaling is done by the runtime (runtimes/python/aletheia_runtime/runtime.py, crates/arx); the program has no endorsement object or issued-set to simplify. An equivalent bug could exist in the Aletheia checker/runtime itself.

Quoting of untrusted data into the prompt is done by the runtime (Runtime.draft in runtime.py, arx lib.rs), not by the program or host. NOTE: the current Aletheia runtime does NOT neutralize <<< >>> or '#' headers at all, so the Aletheia baseline already has the post-mutation behaviour; no faithful mutation exists. An equivalent bug is not just possible but present in the runtime.

Same debugging leftover: the observation is passed to the planner as a plain field instead of quote(...) (the labeled, delimited untrusted-data section). As in the Python, where fields() feeds both plan calls, both the first proposal and the retry are changed.

The budget check is runtime arithmetic (Meter.reserve in runtime.py; arx budget meter); the program only declares `budget [tok <= …, usd <= …]` and cannot express an AND of limits. An equivalent bug could exist in the Aletheia runtime.

The worst-case forecast (est_in + max_out + reasoning) and the provider cap are both computed by the runtime (_sample in runtime.py, providers.py) from the model contract; setting reasoning=0 in the contract would shrink the call cap too, so it is not the same mistake. An equivalent bug could exist in the runtime.
The hash-chained journal is runtime machinery (aletheia_runtime/journal.py, runtime.py line hashing; crates/arx/src/journal.rs). An equivalent bug could exist there.
Effect keys/idempotency and WAL deduplication are generated by the runtime for every commit (runtime.py, wal.py; arx); the program never computes a key. An equivalent bug could exist in the runtime.

Capabilities are minted and checked by the language (Cap[...] typing in athc; values.Cap created by the runtime from the agent signature); program and host code do not construct capabilities. An equivalent bug could exist in the checker/runtime.

The amount shape validation would be the field type in the program, but the Aletheia agent declares amount as plain Text[..16] (the language has no pattern/decimal refinement for Text) and the host already strips commas before float(). So '1,50' already reaches the host and becomes 150 in the Aletheia baseline; there is no validation to widen, and no faithful mutation exists.

The pipeline element (AletheiaAgent.query) is host code; the Runtime holds the host binding (env, FunctionsRuntime, message list, inventories) and provider, so caching it on first use is the same stale-binding mistake.
